after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 6 \\ 14\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
after.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{10\cdot (-2)+6\cdot 1+14\cdot 3}{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}}v=2[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{10\cdot 2+6\cdot (-2)+14\cdot 2}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}w=3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 6 \\ 14\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
content.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{10\cdot (-2)+6\cdot 1+14\cdot 3}{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}}v=2[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{10\cdot 2+6\cdot (-2)+14\cdot 2}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}w=3[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -6 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -12\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}15 \\ -3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
after.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{15\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot 6+(-3)\cdot (-12)}{{3}^{2}+{6}^{2}+(-12)^{2}}v=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -12\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{15\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}w=4[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -12\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}15 \\ -3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
content.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{15\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot 6+(-3)\cdot (-12)}{{3}^{2}+{6}^{2}+(-12)^{2}}v=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -12\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{15\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}w=4[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
after.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{3\cdot 1+2\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 1+1\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3\cdot 2+2\cdot 4+5\cdot 2+1\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3-4)^{2}+(2-2)^{2}+(5-4)^{2}+(1-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
content.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{3\cdot 1+2\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 1+1\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3\cdot 2+2\cdot 4+5\cdot 2+1\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3-4)^{2}+(2-2)^{2}+(5-4)^{2}+(1-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
